subject: Evaluation & Close: Acceptance criteria, exit gates, and test owners for CareBridge MAP
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@carebridge.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@carebridge.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff: Eval objectives + close timeline

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the observability hooks. Before we lock dates I want to confirm what success looks like for our internal stakeholders so we can create a mutual action plan (MAP) that Procurement and Product can sign off on. High-level asks from CareBridge:

- Short POC (6–8 weeks) to validate latency and inference cost under baseline load (10k calls/day).
- Accuracy/concordance checks on 1k de-identified prompts across clinical triage and intake.
- Data handling proof points (audit logs, retention controls).
- Clear exit/acceptance gates so Product knows when to approve a production rollout.

Could you send a draft MAP that maps owners, acceptance tests, and exit gates? Procurement will also need a pointer to your SOC2 evidence and any standard SLA language before they move budget.

Elena Park
Head of Digital Platforms
CareBridge Health

P.S. Looping Samir (Product) for acceptance criteria specifics.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@carebridge.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@carebridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: Eval objectives + close timeline

Elena — thanks for the clear brief. Attaching a one-page MAP and an acceptance-tests draft (see attachments). High-level proposal below; full details are in the attached spreadsheet.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Timeline: Week 0 (kickoff) -> Week 1–4 (integration & smoke) -> Week 5–8 (validation + sign-off) -> Week 9 (decision).
- Owners: Redwood: Marissa (integration + test harness), Camila (security & logs), Markus (deal owner / escalation). CareBridge: Samir (product owner), Elena (executive approver), Procurement contact (budget).
- Acceptance tests (pass/fail):
  - Latency: p95 <= 220 ms for 1–2k concurrent sessions under test workload.
  - Cost: tokens/unit costs within 15% of quoted baseline for steady-state micro-batched traffic.
  - Concordance: >= 88% label agreement on the 1k sample (manual adjudication process described in acceptance-tests.md).
  - Reliability: no more than 1 critical error (5xx or model timeout) per 100k tokens during the validation window.
- Exit gates (fail -> remediation):
  - Gate A (Integration): if no end-to-end flow in 7 days -> roll-back to sandbox and schedule a deep-dive.
  - Gate B (Performance): if p95 > 300 ms for more than 2 consecutive days -> apply auto-scaling and re-run test; if unchanged, pause rollout and open a CAPA.
  - Gate C (Concordance): if concordance < 80% -> stop and run error analysis; optional model tuning/param change allowed once.

Deliverables we will produce during the POC: integration runbook, automated smoke tests, acceptance-tests.md, instrumentation dashboard links, and an evidence packet for Procurement (SOC2 excerpt, audit log sample).

Attachments: map-draft-v1.xlsx; acceptance-tests.md; sla-proposal.pdf

Next step: Marissa will coordinate the integration window. Can you confirm availability for a kickoff on Monday 2028-03-06?

—Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwoodinference.com

Adding operational detail on test ownership and acceptance mechanics. See inline.

Markus — thanks, that aligns with what I expected. A few clarifications to reduce ambiguity during sign-off:

- Test harness & owners:
  - Integration smoke: Marissa (Redwood ENG) + CareBridge dev lead (Samir) — objective: E2E requests to return structured response and pass basic schema checks.
  - Load/latency test: Redwood SRE (SRE team owner) — objective: run Day-1/Day-2 load profile and capture p50/p95/p99.
  - Concordance test: CareBridge clinical SME + Redwood QA (Marissa) — we will run blind adjudication with a 3-person panel; disagreements flagged for review.

- Acceptance-tests.md highlights (excerpt):
  - Test 1 (Schema conformance): 100% pass on 200 sample messages.
  - Test 2 (Latency envelope): p95 <= 220 ms for 95% of test windows over a 24-hour run.
  - Test 3 (Concordance): >= 88% on primary 1k set OR improvement trend of 3% week-over-week during tuning window (whichever occurs first).
  - Test 4 (Data controls): evidence of immutable audit log for all inference requests; retention settable to 90/180/365 days per contract.

- Sign-off process:
  - Product sign-off (Samir): confirms feature-level acceptance.
  - Security sign-off (Camila): validates audit log & encryption controls.
  - Executive sign-off (Elena): greenlights procurement to move to contract.

I also added a short remediation ladder in the spreadsheet for each gate (temporary throttling, model variant fallback, rollback).

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
